title: Greenpill Garden: Season One
dek: Greenpill Garden Season One launched at DevConnect on November 21, 2025: workshops to help stewards build strategy, structure, impact reporting and onchain tools.
excerpt: A steward program planned from DevConnect to April 2026, with workshops on theory of change, cell structures, CIDS and Web3 tools.
body:
On November 12, 2025, Afolabi announced Greenpill Garden Season One on the Regen Coordination Hub. The program grew from a lesson of the previous years: giving stewards money alone does not help them put down deep local roots. Instead, the season offers teaching, support and coordination across many forms of capital, so local initiatives can develop their strategy, funding structure and impact reporting.

The season launched on November 21, 2025, live at DevConnect, with a target end date of April 3, 2026 and a budget of $24,000. Its operators were Afolabi Aiyeloja, Caue Tomaz and Matt Strachman.

## Phases

- Strategy and theory of change (November 21 to December 21): stewards ground their work in a theory of change and the eight forms of capital.
- Structure and protocols (December 22 to January 18): stewards design a cell structure for their initiative.
- CIDS activities and outcomes (January 19 to February 1): stewards map their plans to the Common Impact Data Standard.
- Web3 tooling (February 1 to March 22): stewards put tools to work and report outcomes onchain, with an in-person check-in at ETHDenver.
- Evaluation and retro rewards (March 31 to April 3).

## How it unfolded

In an update on February 11, 2026, Coi reported that Durgadas of GravityDAO had led two strategy workshops with individual feedback on worksheets, that SuperBenefit had hosted a session on cell structures, and that conversations with MetaGov and OpenGrants had explored DAO-IP. Coi described the result so far as clearer shared language and sharper questions rather than a finished design.

The final phase was set to open with Glocal VR's Regenerative Resources Protocol workshop in early March, followed by a Regen Reservoir inventory: a map of what the network's chapters and stewards can offer and what they need.
